name: Warp
license: AGPL-3.0 (client); commercial cloud/orchestration features under Warp product terms

runner.notes: Install Warp Terminal, open only runs/<run-id>/worktree, run the task via Warp Agent and/or a third-party CLI agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI) inside Warp, then harness-verify. Record Warp version, agent harness, model/credits plan, local vs Oz cloud execution, and human interventions separately.

inclusion: Direct Class A ADE: vendor-positioned open-source agentic development environment combining a modern terminal, built-in Warp Agent, third-party CLI agent harnesses, code review, and Oz local/cloud orchestration.
pricing_model: Free terminal tier with limited AI/cloud; paid Build (from ~$20/month with included credits), Max, Business (per-seat), and custom Enterprise. Bring-your-own inference available; agent credits reload pay-as-you-go.
public_stack_signals: Vendor positions Warp as an open-source Agentic Development Environment born out of the terminal.
Client source at warpdotdev/warp; official docs state the client is AGPL v3.
Official docs describe a Rust high-performance terminal with block-based UX, code editor/LSP, and agent modes.
Oz is the orchestration platform for local and cloud agents, multi-model inference, triggers, schedules, and handoff between local and cloud.
Third-party CLI agents officially supported: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, plus built-in Warp Agent and Warp Agent CLI.
capabilities_to_probe: Warp Agent multi-model coding and multi-step task execution
third-party CLI agents inside Warp with shared review/notifications
terminal vs agent modes and multi-session vertical tabs
native code editing, file tree, LSP, and interactive code review comments to agents
worktree/git branch metadata in session UI
Oz cloud agents, local-to-cloud handoff, and concurrent cloud runs
Warp Drive / rules / MCP shared context across local and cloud
enterprise SSO, permission controls, BYOLLM, and self-hosted cloud agents
moat_hypotheses: terminal-native ADE brand with large existing developer install base
open-source client plus commercial Oz cloud orchestration platform
unified surface for first-party Warp Agent and leading third-party coding CLIs
enterprise governance (SOC2, ZDR, SSO, spend caps) around agent fleets
setup_notes: macOS (brew cask), Linux (deb/rpm/AppImage/pacman), and Windows (exe/winget) installers are published on the official site.
Single-task correctness often reflects the selected agent/model more than Warp chrome; record harness dimensions separately.
Do not treat limited free-tier cloud agents as parity with paid Build/Enterprise Oz capacity.

sources.notes: Positioning as open platform for automating development; Warp Terminal ADE claim; Oz platform; Warp Agent; open-source announcement; multi-OS downloads.
Terminal product surface: any-agent workflows, Warp Agent/Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Gemini, multithreaded tabs, native code editing/review, cloud and local agents, enterprise controls.
Getting started: Warp ADE definition, Oz local/cloud agents, multi-model support, AGPL client, SOC2/ZDR privacy claims.
Free/Build/Max/Business/Enterprise credit-based pricing and feature gates.
Open-source client repository linked from official docs and open-source announcement.
Open-source announcement: client open-sourced, community agent-first workflow via Oz, customizable pure-terminal to full ADE modes.

research.positioning: An open-source, terminal-native Agentic Development Environment for running first-party and third-party coding agents locally or in the cloud via Oz, with integrated review, collaboration, and team governance.

runtime: native desktop terminal application (Rust per official docs)
local and cloud coding agents via Oz
third-party CLI agent processes (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI)
frontend: file tree and code editor with LSP
unknowns: Exact closed portions of Oz cloud infrastructure and server-side agent sandbox implementation are not fully published.
Per-agent worktree isolation semantics vs UI git/worktree metadata need hands-on confirmation before parity claims.

infrastructure: Primary surface is a local native terminal ADE on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
Agents run interactively in the local app or as Oz cloud agents on Warp infrastructure or customer self-hosted infrastructure.
Local-to-cloud session handoff is a documented product capability.
Integrations include Slack, Linear, and GitHub triggers for cloud automation.

orchestration: multi-session agent workflows in terminal tabs
Oz local agents for interactive multi-step tasks
Oz cloud agents with triggers, schedules, and parallelism
team session share, review, and steer
workspace_isolation: git branch and worktree metadata in session UI (official terminal marketing)
cloud agents run off-local-machine; isolation model is platform-managed
exact per-task local git worktree policy not fully specified in reviewed docs
review_shipping: native code editing and interactive code review
comments sent back to agents for refinement
cloud agent observability and shareable runs
remote_mobile: cloud agents accessible via Oz platform/dashboard
no first-party mobile ADE app claimed in the reviewed sources
context_memory: MCP servers shared across local and cloud

install_surface: Warp Agent CLI for non-Warp terminals
parity_risks: Free vs paid credit limits change agent capacity mid-run.
Cloud Oz runs are not parity-equivalent to local terminal agent sessions.
Guest third-party CLI quality can dominate single-task correctness.
Worktree isolation must be verified hands-on before claiming parity with worktree-first peers.

hypotheses: Large installed base from terminal product history reduces ADE adoption friction.
Open-source client plus paid Oz/enterprise layer creates a dual open/commercial moat.
First-party agent harness plus third-party CLI toolbelt covers more developer preferences than single-runtime peers.
evidence: Official site and docs explicitly brand Warp as an Agentic Development Environment.
Open-source client and AGPL license are documented on docs.warp.dev and GitHub.
Pricing and enterprise pages list SSO, SOC2, ZDR, BYOLLM, and self-hosted cloud agents.
unknowns: Relative quality of Warp Agent vs Claude Code/Codex on identical tasks is unmeasured in this bench.
Long-term license/commercial boundary between AGPL client and Oz services is only partially described.

research_status: Cataloged 2026-08-10 from official site, docs, pricing, open-source announcement, and GitHub client repo.
